recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore planned/cancelled/abandoned-style Transport.status codes unless OO makes a new decision that reverses the later Event-oriented Transport status model.
issue_request: FHIR-36788 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Transport in R5. It requested a required Transport.status value set containing in-progress, completed, abandoned, cancelled, planned, and entered-in-error, plus an example statusReason value set/code system with declined/refused/not-available/wrong-data/accident/not-acknowledged reasons.
initial_application: The issue was applied through Jira-linked 2022 Transport commits, including 88a67482e7 and cb9bc8aef4. Those updates changed Transport.status, added the transport-status-reason terminology files, and bound Transport.statusReason to the new example value set. Later QA normalization removed generated narrative from the XML but preserved the requested statusReason concepts.
additional_context: Transport is active current-build source in source/fhir.ini. Later final R6 decisions superseded the seed's mixed request/event status list: FHIR-39512 aligned Transport with Event semantics, FHIR-40491 replaced Transport.status with preparation, in-progress, not-done, suspended, stopped, on-hold, completed, entered-in-error, and unknown, and FHIR-50642 rejected adding a pending/planned status because request state belongs on the related Request. FHIR-40749 separately corrected the statusReason CodeSystem name.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already contains the FHIR-36788 statusReason binding and concepts, and the current Transport.status mismatch with the seed's old R5 list is intentional under later final Transport/Event decisions.
